newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. mediator sees Savimbi on Angola peace deal.
newsitem.headline: U.N. mediator sees Savimbi on Angola peace deal.

text.p: United Nations peace mediator Alioune Blondin Beye held talks with veteran guerrilla leader Jonas Savimbi at his bush headquarters in Bailundo on Friday to discuss tensions in Angola's fragile peace process.

Beye told reporters that tensions in relations between the signatories of the 1994 Lusaka peace protocol were based in the former UNITA rebel movement's failure to complete a number of steps by September 20 that were necessary to consolidate peace.
The Angolan government, which fought a nearly 20-year civil war against UNITA since independence from Portugal in 1975, wanted an answer from UNITA on why it had not completed all the steps, he said.
Among these was UNITA's failure to send all of its nine senior generals to the Angolan capital Luanda for integration into a single national army.
Beye said UNITA had also not concluded the disarming of all its 62,500 fighters and failed to complete a selection process of its troops for the Angolan Armed Forces (FAA).
The U.N. has also insisted that UNITA sends back at least some of the 11,000 deserters to the assembly camps where troops are being disarmed.
"The last moments of any peace process are always more difficult and clearly we have reached those last moments," Beye told a news briefing on his return to Luanda.
But he said he had returned from the meeting with Savimbi satisfied that UNITA would complete the last few steps in the peace plan.
"Angolans should continue to believe in the peace process. The war is over," Beye said.
"I am satisfied that the UNITA leadership will complete these steps and I am convinced that peace is still with us."

Beye is to travel to New York next week when the U.N.'s Security Council is scheduled to review its peace-keeping mandate for Angola. About 6,500 U.N. peacekeepers are in the African nation monitoring implementation of the peace accord.
